table_lead: Each rule comes from the tax authority or the law named as its source, checked {checked}. Open a country for the details.
s1_p: Sale amount minus purchase cost. A loss pays no tax.
s2_p: Holding periods (Czechia 3 years, Croatia 2, Germany 1, Austria for coins bought before March 2021) and small-sale limits (Czechia, France, Germany) are checked before any rate.
s3_p: One rate, or progressive bands on your whole tax base (Slovakia, Czechia, Germany): the tax is what the gain adds to the tax on your other income. Spain has its own bands for savings income.
q1: How is tax on a Bitcoin sale calculated?
a1: Take the sale amount, subtract what you paid (fees included), and apply your country's rate to the gain. Some countries tax the gain at one rate (Poland 19%, Austria 27.5%, France 31.4%), others add it to your other income and tax it in bands (Slovakia, Czechia, Germany, Spain).
q2: In which countries is a Bitcoin sale tax-free?
a2: Slovenia does not tax private gains. Czechia exempts coins held more than 3 years, Croatia more than 2, Germany more than 1. In Austria, coins bought before March 2021 and held over a year are tax-free. The Netherlands taxes your wealth on 1 January, not the sale.
q3: Is swapping Bitcoin for another crypto taxed?
a3: It depends on the country. Slovakia, Germany, Czechia and Spain tax a swap like a sale; Poland, France, Austria and Hungary do not. This calculator only handles a sale for euros.
q4: What does the calculator leave out?
a4: Your other sales in the year (annual limits are applied to this sale alone), losses from earlier years, church tax and solidarity surcharge in Germany, and each country's own details listed under the result. It is one sale by a private person in tax year 2026.
a5: No. It shows the arithmetic of the published rule and its source. Before you file, check your case with a tax adviser in your country.
disclaimer: Indicative calculation for one sale by a private person, tax year 2026, with the rules as of {checked}. Not tax advice. Rules marked “not yet” have not been reviewed by a tax adviser.

note_cz: Yearly limits count all your crypto sales: the CZK 100,000 small-sales limit and the CZK 40 million cap on the 3-year exemption. Here this sale is counted alone.
CZK limits converted at the ECB rate of {fxdate}: 1 EUR = {fx} CZK. The 23% band starts at a tax base of CZK 1,762,812.
note_sk: The 16% health insurance on the gain is settled by your health insurer after the year (8% with a disability). Whether it applies in your case, for example as a pensioner, is a question for a tax adviser.
A crypto loss cannot be deducted from your salary or carried into the next year. Gains and losses on crypto sales in the same year are netted, but this calculator handles one sale.

The levy and the tax are both calculated on the full gain. The law treats the health-insurance premium as an expense that should reduce the tax base, but that circular step has not been verified against an official worked example, so the calculator does not apply it yet. Treat the result as an estimate.
note_pl: The 4% solidarity levy on income above PLN 1 million was not checked.
note_at: Austrian providers withhold the tax; sales through foreign exchanges go on your return.
Staking and airdrops are taxed on sale at zero acquisition cost.
note_de: Rates from § 32a EStG for 2026, single filer. Solidarity surcharge and church tax are not included.
The €1,000 limit counts all your private sales in the year. At €1,000 or more the whole gain is taxed.
note_hu: Small transactions (each up to 10% of the minimum wage, one minimum wage a year in total) can be tax-free; not applied here.
A loss declared in a return can be offset against later years.
note_si: The 25% crypto tax proposed in 2025 was not enacted (checked {checked}).
note_hr: A tax-free sale still goes on the JOPPD form by the end of February.
note_ro: Gains of up to 200 lei per sale (600 lei a year) are exempt, and the health contribution (CASS) may apply above income thresholds. Neither is applied here.
note_bg: A 10% deemed-expense reduction may lower the effective rate to about 9%; not applied here.
note_fr: The gain here is sale minus cost. When you sell part of your crypto, France spreads the cost across your whole portfolio (form 2086), so the real gain can differ.
The €305 limit counts all disposals in the year. Crypto-to-crypto swaps are deferred.
note_es: Counted without other savings income (interest, dividends, other gains); with it, more of the gain falls into higher bands. Your salary is taxed on a separate scale.
Model 721 if you hold more than €50,000 in crypto with providers abroad.
